IR.rationale: Rising short-rate expectations relative to the policy rate tighten funding and hurt carry and levered relative-value books. A state of no tightening shock is supportive.

B.rationale: Hedge-fund returns load on credit and liquidity risk. Stable or falling HY and EM corporate yields mark easy credit conditions that favour event-driven, distressed and arbitrage strategies.

V.rationale: News-based financial-crisis volatility captures funding and liquidity stress. Such stress depresses subsequent returns of levered and illiquid strategies.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equities without a value rotation signal a risk-on, growth-led market. Hedge funds with net long equity beta and EM exposure tend to keep earning in that state.

TF.rationale: High payoffs to short-rate trend straddles indicate large unexpected moves in rates. Such moves are associated with deleveraging and weak returns outside CTAs.

ST.rationale: A flight to quality combined with poor reversal returns signals scarce liquidity provision. That environment is adverse for crowded hedge-fund equity positions.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar together with a strong commodity/carry currency reflects easy global dollar funding and risk appetite. Both benefit hedge-fund returns.

COM.rationale: Rising copper prices proxy global growth momentum, which supports risk assets and macro and EM strategies.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions combined with weak activity signal a stress regime. In that regime leverage is costly and redemptions force selling.

ENDG.rationale: Hedge-fund index returns are persistent because of illiquid-asset smoothing and slow-moving capital, so recent strength tends to continue.

IR.rationale: Abrupt rises in bill rates tighten funding and raise the risk of forced deleveraging and tail losses.

B.rationale: Joint widening of European HY and EM corporate yields signals a broad credit sell-off. Such sell-offs precede drawdowns in credit-sensitive and arbitrage strategies.

V.rationale: Elevated equity volatility together with commodity-market turbulence marks a high-uncertainty regime. In that regime the left tail of hedge-fund returns fattens.

AP.rationale: Weak US and EM equities together signal a global risk-off phase. Hedge-fund losses cluster in such phases through beta and liquidity exposure.

TF.rationale: Large short-rate trend payoffs reflect rate shocks, which tend to trigger relative-value and carry unwinds.

ST.rationale: Quality outperformance with failing reversal profits indicates liquidity withdrawal and crowded-trade stress, which raises crash risk.

FX.rationale: A strengthening dollar tightens global dollar funding and is associated with risk-off episodes and EM stress.

COM.rationale: Falling oil and copper together signal weakening global demand. That hurts energy-linked credit, EM exposure and macro positioning.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions in a weak economy are the classic precursor of funding-liquidity spirals and large hedge-fund losses.

ENDG.rationale: Weak recent returns persist and trigger redemptions and forced deleveraging, so poor recent performance raises the chance of a further large loss.

IR.rationale: Absent tightening expectations, funding stays cheap, which supports levered strategies' upside.

B.rationale: Falling risky corporate yields mark credit rallies. Distressed, event-driven and arbitrage funds earn outsized gains in such rallies.

V.rationale: High volatility raises dispersion and the subsequent recovery premium. That benefits CTAs, macro funds and post-stress rebounds in arbitrage spreads.

AP.rationale: A strong, growth-led global equity rally lifts directional and EM-exposed strategies into their right tail.

TF.rationale: Calm short-rate markets without rate shocks allow carry and relative-value trades to compound.

ST.rationale: No flight to quality means risk appetite is intact, which favours the junk and high-beta exposures of hedge funds.

FX.rationale: A strong carry/commodity currency without disorderly currency trends marks a benign risk-on carry regime.

COM.rationale: Copper strength signals global reflation, which supports macro, EM and cyclical exposures.

MC.rationale: Elevated stress implies cheapened assets and wide arbitrage spreads. Subsequent normalisation can deliver large rebound gains.

ENDG.rationale: Return persistence from smoothing and capital inflows makes strong recent performance predictive of further large gains.
